messages.text: I’ll inspect the policy and architecture guidance first, then trace the checked-in benchmark and SlopCop assets to pick three workloads with concrete source edits and observable invalidation effects. I’ll keep this read-only and won’t run benchmarks.

The repository has two likely sources of realistic candidates: checked-in benchmark workloads and the built-in policy packs. I’m checking their publication scope and whether each candidate’s result can be tied to a specific in-repository method edit, rather than relying on a query that only happens to return a fixed identifier.

One routed instruction also applies because the candidates must be publishable: the repository distinguishes open-core content from internal-only benchmark notes and fixtures. I’m reading that boundary now and then will compare the Rust code-smell rules with the actual self-repository source locations.

The evidence points to an important constraint: public policy assets exist, but the strongest cross-file and deep-flow examples are either private benchmark/test material or require endpoint configuration that this checkout does not contain. I’m verifying exact paths and method names now so the handback can distinguish solid candidates from near-misses without presenting fixtures as real workloads.

I’ve narrowed the main constraint: the strongest deep-flow rules either have no production callsites in this checkout or depend on an absent endpoint-set, while the obvious structural hit may live in private `src/bin` code. I’m checking publication boundaries and existing production callsites now; I’ll return concrete, fixed-rule candidates with explicit fit gaps instead of inventing workload hits or running validation.

Understood: the measured corpus is now Tract, so I’m switching candidate discovery there and keeping Bifrost as the source of fixed public rules. I’ll inspect the pinned checkout’s current HEAD and source text only, then give three concrete workloads and edit points; I won’t run the analyzer, MCP, tests, builds, or benchmarks.
Handed back the three Tract candidates, edit anchors, and deep-flow pilot gates. No files were changed and no workloads were run.
